subject: QuantFuse technical recap: latency & throughput targets + deployment options
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@quantfuse.ai>, Ben Rogers <ben.rogers@quantfuse.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2029 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: QuantFuse technical recap: latency & throughput targets + deployment options

Hi Samira / Ben —

Thanks again for the sync earlier today. Quick recap so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive:

Summary of pain & goals
- Customer pain: real-time pricing pipeline under heavy load with bursty traffic, currently hitting 400–600ms p95 and frequent tail spikes.
- Business goal: reduce inference p95 to <= 150ms most of the time, support baseline 2k–3k req/min with burst to 10k for short windows, and keep per-token cost reasonable while retaining deterministic outputs for pricing decisions.

Technical constraints discussed
- Model: preference for open LLaMA-style 7B quantized variant (FP16/4-bit) with 8k context for session history.
- Quality: must preserve existing scoring fidelity; re-eval on our standard prompt suite required.
- Security: customer requires private VPC deployment or Dedicated with strict network controls; SOC2 evidence will be requested.

Initial SLO targets you asked for
- Latency: P95 <= 150ms for inference only (model forward), P99 budget 350ms.
- Throughput: 2,000 req/min sustained, with autoscaling to handle bursts up to 10k req/min for 3–5 minutes.
- Availability: 99.9% monthly, with failover to a cheaper compatible model if capacity constrained.

Deployment options we discussed
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for predictable throughput & private networking.
- Redwood Private (VPC) for air-gapped/regulatory needs — will require on-prem or partner-hosted nodes.
- Routing: smart routing + KV prefix-caching to reduce per-token compute for repeated session prefixes.

Attachments: I attached a draft SLO matrix and a high-level deployment sketch.

Next steps (owner / ETA)
- QuantFuse: confirm peak burst windows and provide anonymized sample traffic histogram (Ben) — by EOD Thu.
- Redwood: run quick cost/throughput sketch for 7B quantized on dedicated T4-like config and share numbers (Karthik) — by Fri.
- Schedule 60m technical deep-dive with ops + infra (both sides) — proposed Tue 25 Jun, I’ll send a calendar invite.

If any of the above is off, flag it and I’ll correct. Otherwise we’ll use this as the agenda for the next call.

Thanks,
Priya

Subject: Re: QuantFuse technical recap: latency & throughput targets + deployment options

Thanks Priya — solid summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Burst profile: typical day has micro-bursts (~500 req/min) but three main windows (market open, close, midday spikes) where we hit ~8k–12k for 2–6 minutes. I will extract a 7‑day histogram and drop it in the Drive link by Thursday.

2) Model fidelity: our scoring is sensitive to tokenization differences; we need the same tokenizer and a deterministic seed for reranks in the pricing loop. Can you confirm Redwood supports pinned tokenizer/version and deterministic sampling for rerank pipelines?

3) Security: procurement asked for a high-level cost worksheet and SOC2 attestation before we show the platform to our security team. Can you provide those materials?

We’re good with the suggested next steps — Tue 25 Jun works for the deep-dive. Thanks,
Ben
Ben Rogers
Head of Product, QuantFuse
ben.rogers@quantfuse.ai

Subject: RE: QuantFuse technical recap: latency & throughput targets + deployment options (technical notes)

Ben / Samira / team —

Adding technical detail from our infra side so you have what you need for planning the deep-dive: 

Short answers to Ben’s questions
- Tokenizer/version pinning: yes — we can pin tokenizer artifacts to the model bundle and expose exact hashes in the model manifest. Deterministic rerank sampling: supported via deterministic beam/greedy decode or fixed RNG seed in production pipelines.
- SOC2 / attestation: Redwood will provide SOC2 Type II report and a short security brief; I’ll attach pointers in the drive folder.

Proposed deployment topology (prioritized)
1) Dedicated - colocated GPU pools (preferred for predictable p95):
   - 4 x A10s (or equivalent) in a dedicated pool per region for primary, autoscale with warm spare nodes.
   - Continuous batching with KV prefix cache to reduce compute for repeated session prefixes; cache hit expected ~25–40% based on similar customers.
   - Per-request routing policy: P95-sensitive requests go to low-latency zone; non-critical bulk scoring to lower-cost nodes.

2) Private VPC (for compliance):
   - Customer-managed subnets with Redwood control plane peering.
   - Option: small on-prem inference cluster + burst to Redwood Dedicated when allowed.

Performance estimates (rough, to be validated in poc)
- 7B quantized (4-bit) — single request latency: ~80–120ms forward on an A10 with optimized kernels for short prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Throughput: a 4 x A10 pool with batching should comfortably handle 2k–3k req/min sustained with headroom; bursts to 10k require short-lived burst capacity (extra nodes + autoscaler tuning).
- Cost: preliminary unit cost estimate attached in the spreadsheet; we’ll refine after we get your exact token distribution and prompt lengths.

Observability & fallbacks
- We’ll instrument token-level latency, cache hit rates, and per-route SLO dashboards.
- Fallback policy: automatic failover to a smaller/cheaper compatible model variant (e.g., 3B quant) if utilization exceeds thresholds to preserve latency SLOs.

Ask for your team before the deep-dive
- Sample prompt & average prompt length (tokens).
- 7-day traffic histogram (Ben) + expected max sustained burst duration.
- Any hard network egress restrictions if planning VPC/on-prem.

I’ll put an updated topology sketch + the kernel tuning notes in Drive now.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
